ops.title: container-hermes supervisor + egress pf: codex security review outcomes (2026-07-18)
ops.body:
Two adversarial codex (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) reviews of the container-native hermes Phase-2 stack. Synthesis/accept-reject by the fable orchestrator. Plan: z-4-virtual-generic-lampson. pf design: [[container-hermes egress pf (2e): design, ordering, and posture options]] (note 9623c9a). Prototype verdict: note 4656afb.

## pf ruleset review (scripts/host/container-pf.sh) — STRONG PASS

- **Interaction A (anchor ordering vs host-pf's unscoped model-port pass): CONFIRMED SOUND.** codex grounded it in XNU `pf.c` (`pf_test_rule`/`pf_step_out_of_anchor`): a `quick` match inside a nested anchor terminates the ENTIRE filter traversal — later sibling anchors + main ruleset never see the packet. So `000.yclaw.container`'s terminal `block drop ... quick`, evaluating alphabetically before `000.yclaw.host`, means host-pf's unscoped `pass in ... from {metal} to any port <ports>` (host-pf.sh:144) can never adjudicate a container-bridge packet. Alphabetical-first ordering is load-bearing and correct. codex also flagged that scoping host-pf:144 with `on $VMNET_IF` would be a red-herring no-op (wrong bridge).
- **Interaction B (`to any` self-leak): SOUND** — flat tier-1-before-tier-2 ordering correctly carves self/private out of the `to any` passes.
- **APPLIED fixes:** (#2b) added `NEED_KILL` + `pfctl -k "$CNET"` on rule change / empty anchor (state survives a rule reload otherwise); (#3) interface resolution now requires exactly one UP bridge carrying the gateway (apple/container's unclean shutdowns can strand a stale bridge, #1321).
- **ACCEPTED tradeoff (not a defect):** (#1) tier-2 is a general public-egress channel — the user explicitly chose the MODERATE posture (443/DNS-to-any) over Strict, knowing a compromised agent can still exfil over 443. Strict (pin tailscale CIDRs) is the documented follow-up.
- **DECLINED:** (#4) DHCP dst:68 breadth — kept for parity with host-pf + bootstrap safety on an untestable path.

## Supervisor chain review — codex verdict: "do NOT load this chain as-is" (1 Critical + 4 High)

APPLIED (clearly-correct): (#8) setup now creates `$STATE_DIR/hermes` (apple/container rejects a nonexistent bind → clean deploy failed at `container run`); (#10) gid-safety assertions (refuse a drifted gid or a squatter on gid 1000).

STILL OPEN — blockers / design decisions (NOT auto-fixed; surfaced to user):
- **#1 CRITICAL — symlink TOCTOU host-escape in the proxy's bind-SOURCE validation (policy.go).** Agent symlinks a path inside the allowed root, passes `EvalSymlinks`, flips it to `/` before apple/container resolves it → nested container mounts the host FS, reads sops key. NOTE: this is in hermes-docker-proxy (the SAME proxy the live tart hermes uses) → pre-existing, not a migration regression, but Architecture B makes the sandbox path load-bearing. Fix is a bind-policy redesign (allow only fixed broker-owned roots, mount the whole root; pathname validation cannot authorize agent-renamable descendants). NEEDS a refuter pass (is it exploitable through all layers?) + a design decision before touching it.
- **#2 HIGH — gid 1000 may NOT propagate into the GUEST socket.** codex (reading apple/container 1.1.0 `RuntimeService.swift` + containerization 0.35.0 `VsockProxy.swift`) claims apple/container copies only the host socket's MODE bits, not uid/gid, and vminitd creates the guest staging socket root-owned — so a `root:root 0660` guest socket is NOT connectable by the dropped uid/gid 1000, and the tick's gid-1000 guard checks the WRONG side of the mount. OVERTURNS the design premise. codex flagged it needs INDEPENDENT EMPIRICAL verification against the installed version (it's source-reading, not tested). Robust fix if true: entrypoint `chgrp 1000 + chmod 0660` the guest socket + a uid-1000 connect probe before drop — but that means REBUILDING the image. VERIFY LIVE at bring-up before rebuilding.
- **#3/#4/#5 HIGH — the tick treats existence/liveness as correctness.** `container_running` matches only the name (a stale/misconfigured `hermes` container is trusted); `wait_path_exists` passes against a stale/wrong/symlink socket node; `pgrep -f` is an unanchored regex (another process with the binary path in argv → false match → skip relaunch; codex confirmed the tick itself + `tail -f` are NOT live risks). codex's key recommendation: ONE in-container canary — a forbidden request through the mounted proxy socket requiring the proxy-specific 403 — proves the agent talks to the FILTERING proxy (not raw socktainer) and closes most of #3+#4. Plus: `test -S` + owner/mode/gid on the socket; anchored/escaped pgrep or separate launchd jobs.

FOLLOW-UPS (lower urgency): #6 per-command deadlines (needs `gtimeout`; StartInterval REJECTED — dead on Tahoe) + wire the `.last-ok` markers into `yclaw doctor`; #7 `setup host-container` rebuilds the proxy binary but doesn't restart the running one (operator thinks a hardening update is live when it isn't); #9 document the login-account/repo trust boundary in the sudo helper; #11 proxy HTTP server has no ReadHeaderTimeout/IdleTimeout/conn cap (agent can exhaust it).

CONFIRMED SOUND by codex: no socket-path confusion in the serial tick; mount set has no overlapping targets; `:ro` correct; socket mounted rw is correct for the relay; setgid-dir group inheritance works (losing setgid alone is not load-bearing, changing the dir group is); targeted `pfctl -a -f` never flushes vmnet NAT.
